info.name: ADD OS — Identity & Content
info.description:
Member app auth (phone + password, with WhatsApp OTP for sign-up and recovery), Ops dashboard auth (Fortify session + 2FA, Sanctum SPA), admin-managed site content (Founders/Partners/Community), and the public read-only feed of that same content.

Import the companion environment (ADD OS - Local) and select it — base_url, admin_email, admin_password, member_phone, member_password all live there.

Everything under /api lives under /api/v1 — the whole API is versioned from day one.

Before using Admin/*: run the app locally with `php artisan serve --port=8000` — Sanctum's stateful-domain check only recognizes 127.0.0.1:8000 by default.

Member sign-up (once): Member/Auth/Register — Send Code (validates the whole profile up front) → read the code from storage/logs/laravel.log (mock WhatsApp driver) → Member/Auth/Register — Verify & Create. Member sign-in (every time after): Member/Auth/Login. Both capture an access_token + refresh_token pair into {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}}; the access token expires after 60 minutes, and Member/Auth/Refresh Token renews it. Forgot the password? Forgot Password → Reset Password → Login.

Admin flow: Admin/Auth/Get CSRF Cookie once, then Admin/Auth/Login — every other Admin/* request reads the XSRF token from the cookie jar automatically. Each Admin/Content/* "Create" request captures the new row's id into a variable ({{founder_id}}, {{partner_id}}, {{community_member_id}}) so the Get/Update/Delete requests right below it work with no manual editing.

item.name: Member (App)
item.description: Phone + password → Sanctum bearer token, with a WhatsApp code (mock driver for now) gating sign-up and password recovery.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
MEMBERS ONLY. An operations or admin account cannot sign in or reset a password anywhere in this folder — those accounts belong to Admin/Auth, behind Fortify's second factor. Tokens minted here carry the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects, so this surface stays sealed off from operations even for someone who is legitimately both.

Two separate journeys, in order.

SIGN UP (once per member): Register — Send Code → Register — Verify & Create. Step 1 validates the whole profile and parks it, so a number that already has an account is refused there with a 422 rather than after the OTP round trip; step 2 then needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` until step 2.

SIGN IN (every time after): Login with phone + password. Refresh Token renews the access token when it expires (60 min) without re-entering the password; Logout ends the session on this device only.

FORGOT IT: Forgot Password → Reset Password. The reset revokes every token the member holds on every device, and deliberately issues none — sign in again afterwards.

Register — Verify & Create, Login and Refresh Token all capture the pair into {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}}.

request.description:
Step 1 of sign-up. Validates the ENTIRE profile first and only then sends the code — so "this number already has an account", "that email is taken" and "password too short" all come back as 422 here, before you spend a WhatsApp message and an OTP round trip on a sign-up that was never going to succeed.

On success the profile is parked in `pending_registrations` (password already hashed) so step 2 needs only the phone and the code. Nothing lands in `users` — an unverified sign-up is never an account. The parked row expires with its code after 5 minutes and is swept hourly by `model:prune`, so abandoning the flow leaves nothing behind and holds no phone number.

Running this again overwrites the parked profile, which is how you correct a typo: fix the field, re-send, use the new code.

There is no `purpose` field — this endpoint always mints a `registration` code, and Forgot Password always mints a `password_reset` one. A code issued by one is refused by the other with an explicit 422; they are not interchangeable.

Rate-limited (1 per cooldown window per phone per purpose, plus a 10/min per-IP throttle). Code is dispatched via the mock WhatsApp driver — check storage/logs/laravel.log for the value until a real gateway is wired up.

Step 2 of sign-up, and ACCOUNT CREATION ONLY — this is no longer the repeat login the old otp/verify was. Returning members use Login.

Just the phone and the code. The profile was validated and parked at step 1, so nothing is re-typed and the password crosses the wire only once. Creates the account, assigns the 'member' role, provisions an empty wallet, and discards the parked row — all in one transaction.

Returns an access_token + refresh_token pair, both captured automatically. The access token carries the ability `member-app` and nothing more, so it cannot reach /api/v1/admin/* even if the same person is also an operator.

422 "please start signing up again" means there is no parked profile — step 1 was never run, or it expired along with its code (both last 5 minutes). Re-run step 1.

409 means the number or email was free at step 1 and got claimed in between — a race, not the normal "already registered" answer, which step 1 gives you as a 422.

The everyday sign-in, for MEMBERS ONLY. Returns the same access_token + refresh_token pair sign-up does, both captured automatically. The token carries the ability `member-app`, which /api/v1/admin/* rejects.

401 is deliberately identical for three different failures — wrong password, unregistered number, and an account that holds no `member` role (an operations or admin account). Operators sign in at Admin/Auth/Login, behind Fortify's second factor; if this endpoint issued them a token, phone + password alone would reach the operations API and the second factor would be worth nothing. The wording is shared so the response can't be used to work out which numbers have accounts, or which of those belong to staff.

403 means the account is deactivated or blocked; no token is issued and the body names the state.

429 after 5 attempts per minute for this phone+IP combination, with retry_after in the body.

Renews an expired access token without the password. Unauthenticated — the refresh token in the body IS the credential.

Single use: the token sent here is revoked and the previous access token deleted, so both variables are overwritten with the replacements. Sending the same refresh token twice returns 401.

Also 401 if the refresh token has expired (30 days) or the account was deactivated/blocked in the meantime.

Sends a `password_reset` code. Always answers 200 with the same neutral message whether or not the number has an account — that is intentional, and means a 200 here is not confirmation that anything was sent.

A registered number gets the code via the mock WhatsApp driver: read it from storage/logs/laravel.log and paste it into Reset Password.

Sets the new password and revokes every access and refresh token the member holds, on every device — the old password may already be compromised, so nothing opened under it survives.

Issues no token on purpose: run Login afterwards with the new password. {{member_token}} and {{member_refresh_token}} are stale until you do.

The code must have been issued by Forgot Password. A sign-up code sent here is refused with 422 and a message saying so.
Revokes the current access token. Calling Account/Get Me again afterwards should return 401.

item.name: Account
item.description: Anything about the already-authenticated member, as opposed to the act of logging in.

item.name: Company
item.description: Self-service for a company's own admin managing their own company's members — gated by CompanyPolicy::manageMembers (is_admin on the company_user pivot), checked in the controller rather than by role middleware. Adding or removing a member entirely stays operations-only (Admin (Dashboard)/Company Members).

request.description: 403 if the acting member isn't an admin of this specific company.
403 if the acting member isn't already an admin of this specific company.

Updates the authenticated member's stored language preference (`ar`/`en`). Distinct from the `lang` header: the header overrides the response language for this one request; this changes what a future request with no header falls back to.

Updates the authenticated member's stored currency preference (`USD`/`SYP`, display-only — never affects real pricing/wallet records). Distinct from the `currency` header: the header overrides a plan-listing response's converted currency for this one request; this changes the stored default a request with no header falls back to.

Returns the authenticated member in one payload: the same account fields as Get Me (id, name, phone, email, preferred_language, preferred_currency, status, roles) plus `personal` (`bio`, `city`, `avatar_url`) and `professional` (`job_title`, `company_name`, `industry`, `linkedin_url`). Profile fields are null until the member has ever saved one — there is no separate "not found" state; the underlying rows are only created on first PATCH. Independent of `Account → Get Me`, which stays account-info-only.

Upserts the personal AND professional profile in one call, in one transaction — creates both rows on first call, updates them after, never a duplicate row on either table. Every field is optional and independently nullable: omitting a field leaves it unchanged, sending it as `null` explicitly clears it. Send all seven fields together (as in this example) or just the subset you're changing — both work. Plain single-language strings, not the `{ar, en}` bilingual JSON pattern used for admin-curated content. Returns the same combined shape as Get Profile.

Returns whether the authenticated member currently has an active `public_directory` consent grant: `{"granted": true|false}`. A member who never granted, or who revoked and never re-granted, gets `false`.

Grants (`granted: true`) or revokes (`granted: false`) the member's consent to appear in the public member directory (see Public (Site) → Get Member Directory). Consent is append-only history: granting while already active is a no-op, revoking sets `revoked_at` on the active row, and re-granting after a revoke inserts a fresh row rather than reusing the old one. Appearing in the directory also requires at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional) and an `active` account status.

Ingests a client-reported error/crash from the member mobile app. Lives under mobile.php, not member.php — deliberately UNAUTHENTICATED (no bearer token needed): a crash can happen before login, e.g. on the splash/login screen itself, so this can't depend on a session existing yet. Placed here for discoverability alongside the rest of the mobile app's requests. Only `error_type` and `message` are required; everything else is optional context. `platform` is restricted to `android`/`ios`; `occurred_at` defaults to now() if omitted. Throttled at 60/min per IP.

item.name: Admin (Dashboard)
item.description: Fortify (session + 2FA) + Sanctum SPA. Public registration is disabled on purpose — accounts are created by an existing admin (see database/seeders/AdminUserSeeder.php for the first one).

item.name: Auth
item.description: The login lifecycle: CSRF cookie, login (with optional 2FA challenge), log out.

request.description: Run this first — sets the XSRF-TOKEN cookie that every other request in Admin/* reads automatically.
Returns {"two_factor": false} and logs the session in directly if 2FA isn't confirmed yet, or {"two_factor": true} and expects Two-Factor Challenge next.
Only needed if Login responded with two_factor: true. Use {"recovery_code": "..."} instead of "code" to fall back to a recovery code.

item.name: Account
item.description: Anything about the already-authenticated admin/staff user.

request.description: Guarded by role:admin|operations — a logged-in member-only account gets 403 here, not 401. Also blocked (403) if the account's own status is deactivated/blocked, even with a fully valid session — see EnsureAuthenticatedUserIsActive.

item.name: Two-Factor Authentication
item.description: Setup and management of TOTP 2FA — separate from Auth because these calls happen while already logged in, not while logging in.

request.description: Generates a secret + recovery codes but leaves 2FA unconfirmed until Confirm succeeds.
Code from an authenticator app scanning the QR code above. Once confirmed, future logins require Auth/Two-Factor Challenge.

item.name: Password
item.description: Password confirmation gate, change, and the forgot/reset recovery flow.

request.description: Fortify requires a fresh password confirmation (session-timed) before sensitive actions like changing the password or disabling 2FA.
MAIL_MAILER=log by default — check storage/logs/laravel.log for the reset link/token.

item.name: Private Office Requests
item.description: PRD §5.3 pipeline: requested -> quoted -> contracted. 'contracted' is only reachable through Companies/Create Company below, never through Update here.

request.description: Starts at status 'requested'.
status only accepts "requested" or "quoted" here — a 422 comes back for "contracted", which is only reachable via Companies/Create Company.

item.name: Companies
item.description: Created exclusively by operations from a quoted private-office request (PRD §5.1/§5.3) — never self-service. Creating one also auto-provisions its wallet (Phase 3, out of scope for this collection otherwise).

request.description: 422 if private_office_request_id isn't currently 'quoted' — run Private Office Requests/Mark as Quoted first. branch_id must reference an existing branch.
status must be "active" or "inactive" — anything else is a 422.

item.name: Company Members
item.description: door_access_enabled and is_admin are the only scoped capabilities in the app (D.8). Everything here sits under role:admin|operations; a company's own admin has the equivalent self-service actions under Member (App)/Company.

request.description: is_admin here is how a company gets its very first admin — a company admin can only promote an existing member (CompanyPolicy::manageMembers), so operations has to bootstrap the first one. 422 if user_id is already a member of this company.

item.name: Users
item.description: Operations/admin accounts only — members self-register via Member (App)/Auth (phone + OTP), never through here. status must be active, deactivated, or blocked — the old 'suspended' value no longer exists (see docs/decisions/phase-3-membership-plan-wallet-mechanics.md's sibling audit notes).

request.description: Optional ?role= filter (member/operations/admin).
role must be "operations" or "admin" — this endpoint never creates a plain member. admin-only route (role:admin, not role:admin|operations — an operations account gets 403 here).
Profile fields only — status and role are the two separate actions below.

status must be active, deactivated, or blocked (422 otherwise). Setting deactivated/blocked immediately revokes every access token this user holds (User::deactivate()/block()) — their very next request with an old token comes back 401, not 403. reason is optional but always recorded (status_reason/status_changed_at/status_changed_by).
role must be member, operations, or admin. admin-only route.

item.name: Roles
item.description: Just the assignable role names — no granular permissions yet (D.8).

item.name: Content
item.description: Admin-managed site content — Founders, Partners, Community. Each 'Create' below auto-captures the new row's id for the requests under it.

item.name: Public (Site)
item.description: Unauthenticated reads for the marketing website — only published/active rows are ever returned here.

request.description: Only partners with is_active = true are returned.
Only published = true rows are returned. Enable the ?category= query param to filter by pioneers/growth_partners/investors/impact_partners.

Lists members who have an active `public_directory` consent grant, at least one filled profile (Personal and/or Professional), and an `active` account status. Never includes phone/email regardless of consent. Unauthenticated, paginated (20 per page, ordered by name), throttled, and computed fresh on every request — no caching.
